title: Building Stack Simulator on Roblox with Codex and Claude Code
author: BerkshireByteaway
selftext:
I'm a mobile game producer building Roblox games as a hobby under Berkshire Byteaway. My project is now called Stack Simulator, previously Delivery to the Moon. You time placements to stack boxes, then use coins for upgrades, grow pets and unlock space destinations.

I use Codex and Claude Code extensively. When I reached a Codex usage limit, I used written handoff documents to continue in Claude Code. I set priorities, playtest builds, give concrete feedback on issues such as unresponsive buttons and overlapping UI, and make the release decisions myself.

For others switching between AI coding tools, what do you include in a handoff to keep track of unfinished work and things that still need testing?

If you'd like to try the game, feedback on the opening instructions and UI would also help: [https://www.roblox.com/games/129540867664812/](https://www.roblox.com/games/129540867664812/)

A Roblox account and client are required. Access is currently restricted to ages 16+.

AI was used extensively in development and helped draft this English post.
